title: Aston Villa’s Amadou Onana targeting return from injury for Europa League final
content:
Amadou Onana is targeting a return for Aston Villa’s Europa League final against Freiburg on May 20.

Onana, who sustained a calf injury in the first leg of the semi-final against Nottingham Forest, was absent in Villa’s 2-2 draw against Burnley on Sunday.

Sources close to the player, speaking on the condition of anonymity, told The Athletic last week that the 24-year-old was aiming to be back fit in the week leading up to the final in Istanbul.

In Onana’s place, Victor Lindelof has impressively filled in alongside Youri Tielemans in midfield. However, Onana is a key player for Unai Emery who admitted after the draw at Turf Moor that he could play again this season.

“Hopefully but I don’t know,” the Spaniard said in his post match press conference. “He is still being injured.

“Firstly, the doctor told us it is more or less three weeks. We are going to be working with Lindelof in this position, we are working hard with Bogarde in this position. We do not have (Boubacar) Kamara, who of course is very important for us. But I am positive with the players we have. In case someone is not available, we will find solutions, like we did always.”

Onana has made 36 appearances across all competitions this season, with Villa in fifth place in the Premier League and four points ahead of Bournemouth, who are the closest to chasing down a Champions League spot.
